---
title: "16 · Proximity graphs"
execute:
  enabled: false
---

When no flow is observed and no street joins two entities, the relation between
them can be posited from geometric closeness. City2Graph offers seven
constructions for points and one for polygons, and which you pick is a
hypothesis about which spatial relation matters, not a neutral preprocessing
step, so the notebook builds all of them over the same points, restaurants and
cafés in one neighborhood: `knn_graph` and
`fixed_radius_graph` for relative and absolute proximity, the four
non-parametric constructions (`delaunay_graph`, `gabriel_graph`,
`relative_neighborhood_graph`, `euclidean_minimum_spanning_tree`), the
probabilistic `waxman_graph`, and `contiguity_graph` for polygons. It closes
with the two layer-coupling tools, `bridge_nodes` and `group_nodes`.

Two divergences are documented where they appear: `generate_proximity_graph`
reduces polygons to points before calling `contiguity_graph()`, so `CONTIGUITY`
always yields zero edges, and `prox_deduplicate`, on by default, rebuilds the
GeoDataFrame and loses columns and the original index. The notebook also detects
a bug in **city2graph 0.3.1** itself: `gabriel_graph()` compares squared
distances against an absolute `1e-12` tolerance, so with UTM coordinates it
returns an incorrect graph (248 edges where there should be 453). The check is
`RNG ⊆ Gabriel`, and a workaround is included.
